Les îles Whitsunday, au large du Queensl: The Whitsunday Islands, off the coast of Queensland, are best discovered by boat. We left from Airlie Beach, the town most cruises depart from, on board a sailing boat run by Matador, for two days and one night at sea.

<b>430 dollars australiens par personne<: 430 Australian dollars per person, for two full days: leaving on Saturday at 8:30 am, back on Sunday at 4 pm.
Les repas sont compris : le déjeuner et: Meals are included: lunch and dinner on Saturday, then breakfast and lunch on Sunday. You do not need to bring anything to eat on board.
<b>Le matériel de snorkeling est compris: Snorkelling gear is included, wetsuit too, and we had nothing extra to pay on the spot.
Pas de boissons particulières incluses e: No special drinks are included on top of the meals, but you can bring your own food and drinks on board.
<b>Whitehaven Beach.</b> Premier grand a: Whitehaven Beach. The first big stop, and we climbed up to the Hill Inlet lookout to see what is often called the most beautiful beach in the world. Unfortunately, the weather was not on our side that day: be ready for it to work against you, that is the lottery of every cruise.
Les tourbillons de sable blanc de Hill I: The swirls of white sand at Hill Inlet seen from above, at the end of Whitehaven Beach
<b>Trois spots de snorkeling sur la Gran: Three snorkelling spots on the Great Barrier Reef, one after another on Sunday morning. This is the heart of the cruise: we saw a Napoleon wrasse, turtles and a huge amount of coral. They are among the most beautiful snorkelling spots I have ever done, and one of the most memorable moments of my road trip. We had a wetsuit to get in the water. In October, the jellyfish in the Whitsundays are not dangerous, but check with the crew if you go at another time of year.
<b>La soirée du samedi</b> n'a rien d'ex: Saturday evening is nothing special: a bit of music on deck, time to get to know each other, and everyone goes to bed fairly early. It is very simple, and that is also the charm of a night at sea.
On était un groupe d'une vingtaine de pa: We were a group of about twenty passengers, with three or four crew members. The atmosphere is friendly, and it is easy to get to know people when you share the same deck for two days.
Les passagers installés sur le pont du v: Passengers relaxing on the deck of the sailing boat, seen from above
If you get seasick, be warned. A sailing boat moves a lot more than a big motor boat, and at one point the sea got rough and it really rocked. Bring something to help if you are sensitive to it.

<b>La nuit à bord</b>, tout le monde dor: At night, everyone sleeps together in the hold of the boat. As for facilities, there are two toilets and two showers for about twenty people: showers are very quick.
Le dimanche, réveil tous ensemble, puis: On Sunday, everyone wakes up together, then the morning of snorkelling before heading back to Airlie Beach.
<b>Les repas</b> sont de bonne qualité,: The meals are good quality, but simple. Do not expect fine dining, rather generous, well made dishes for a day at sea.

<b>On a roulé de Sydney vers Cairns, mai: We drove from Sydney to Cairns, but I recommend the opposite. If you leave in October, start in Cairns and head south to Sydney. Up north, the good season is coming to an end in October, while in the south the warm days are arriving. <b>Partir sur la boucle de Thakhek sans: Setting off on the Thakhek loop without planning for fuel. Petrol stations are far apart, and on some stretches you only find jerry cans sold by the roadside.
<b>Oublier que le nord est froid.</b> Be: Forgetting that the north is cold. Many people arrive in Nong Khiaw in tropical clothes and spend the night shivering.
<b>Prendre le scooter sans permis adapté: Riding a scooter without the right licence. As elsewhere in Asia, insurance covers nothing without an international driving permit with the motorbike category.
<b>Ce qu'on a vu, nous.</b> Beaucoup de: What we saw ourselves. A lot of people fell off their scooters on the Thakhek loop. The roads are dangerous in places and it happens fast. Ride carefully, that is the one thing to remember.
Et l'erreur qu'on ne fait qu'une fois :: And the mistake you only make once: not filling up every time you pass a station. Some parts of the loop are deserted, and running out there costs you a lot of time.
Deux réalités dictent le sac au Laos : l: Two realities decide what goes in your bag in Laos: the cool nights in the north, and the dust on the tracks.
<b>Une couche chaude.</b> Le nord est en: A warm layer. The north is at altitude. Between November and February, it can drop below ten degrees at night, while it is thirty during the day in Vientiane.
<b>Un tour de cou et des lunettes.</b> S: A neck gaiter and glasses. On the Thakhek loop as on the northern tracks, the dust never stops. It is the one euro accessory that changes a day on the scooter.
<b>Une lampe frontale.</b> Les grottes d: A head torch. The caves around Thakhek are often visited without lighting, and power cuts are frequent in the villages.
<b>Des espèces.</b> Les distributeurs se: Cash. ATMs are concentrated in the towns. On a loop lasting several days, you need to leave with enough to get by, fuel included.
<b>Côté électrique.</b> Le Laos est en 2: Electricity. Laos runs on 230 volts, with type A, B, C, E and F sockets depending on the building. A universal adapter is really useful here.
<b>Et le conseil qui vaut partout :</b>: And the advice that applies everywhere: pack light. It is true on all my trips, and even more so here, where you switch between backpack and scooter several times.

<b>La carte d'arrivée numérique.</b> Dep: The digital arrival card. Since 1 May 2025, all foreign travellers must fill in the Thailand Digital Arrival Card, the TDAC, online. <b>L'exemption de visa, et le piège du m: The visa exemption, and the current catch. French citizens enter without a visa for tourism, and the stay is currently sixty days, extendable by thirty on the spot for about 1,900 baht. Sauf que cette durée est en sursis. Le g: Except that this duration is on borrowed time. The Thai government approved a return to thirty days in May 2026, then confirmed in July that France was on the list of countries concerned. The measure only comes into force fifteen days after its publication in the Thai Royal Gazette, and that publication still had not happened by mid August 2026.
Autrement dit : au moment où j'écris, c': In other words: as I write, it is still sixty days for French citizens, but it could switch to thirty overnight. If your stay is longer than a month, check the duration in force before you book, on the website of the Thai embassy in your country.
